messages.subject: New theme system
parts:
Hi everyone -

I've been working on the new theme system, based off the ideas Hadley posted a while back. I think it's to the point where it's ready for some feedback. Check it out and let me know if you have any comments or suggestions:

messages.subject: Re: New theme system
parts:
I'm curious what the output of my_theme looks like. You mention that previously it was a mess of functions but now it's a list of lists. 

I'm asking because of this: 

mytheme <- theme_grey()

mytheme$text$family <- "Times"
mytheme$text$colour <-"red"

It seems to me that there should be a better way of modifying individual properties of an element, but it's not obvious to me at this point how to do that.

At least a list of lists is more obvious, as long as the elements (family, color, size) are clear (they seem to be). 

I <3 rel(). 

B

I much prefer the "list of lists" structure to the list of functions. I solves many problems and is easier to apprehend.

A few remarks:

- trying to install I get:

ERROR: package installation failed


- shouldn't title inherit from text? It does not on the graph

- similarly, shouldn't legend.box inherit from rect?

- I don't see a difference between a line and a segment from the point of view of the user. Can they be merged in the UI (even if the grid functions called do actually draw axis ticks or grid lines are actually different)? Since there is no difference visually, to know what to change, the user would have to dive into theme_gray(). If we want to change stuff to keep it simple, this might be a good thing to prune out.

- I don't see a mechanism to force inheritance. Let us say I want all my lines to be black, because I intend to print in black and white purely. My first instinct would be to do
line = element_line(colour = "black")
but that does not change anything since this is already the default. Meanwhile, grid lines would still be white because the colour is specified at a lower level (panel.grid.major).
I would be nice, if feasible, to have something like the !important property in CSS, which overrides inheritance, like
line = element_line(colour = force("black"))
and now every line is black. Or even assume force() by default when using element_* functions : since the user is modifying the theme, he/she probably wants the instructions to be effective no matter what. There is still the possibility of direct access through the list for smaller modifications.

- some text properties seem to be used only in legend: justification, align. Would it make sense to have them for all text elements (i.e. I want my axis labels to be left-aligned instead of centered)?

parts: On Tue, May 29, 2012 at 5:38 AM, Brandon Hurr <brando...@gmail.com> wrote:

I'm curious what the output of my_theme looks like. You mention that previously it was a mess of functions but now it's a list of lists. 

I'm asking because of this: 

mytheme <- theme_grey()

mytheme$text$family <- "Times"
mytheme$text$colour <-"red"
mytheme$text$size   <- 16

It seems to me that there should be a better way of modifying individual properties of an element, but it's not obvious to me at this point how to do that.

At least a list of lists is more obvious, as long as the elements (family, color, size) are clear (they seem to be).

The themes objects actually are list of lists. 

The element functions return lists with class element_xx:

> str(element_text(family="Times", face="bold", colour="black", size=12))
List of 8
 $ family    : chr "Times"
 $ face      : chr "bold"
 $ colour    : chr "black"
 $ size      : num 12
 $ hjust     : NULL
 $ vjust     : NULL
 $ angle     : NULL
 $ lineheight: NULL
 - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_text"


 And a theme just is a list of these things (although some of the element items are just strings):

d> str(theme_grey())
List of 39
 $ line                :List of 3
  ..$ colour  : chr "black"
  ..$ size    : num 0.5
  ..$ linetype: num 1
  ..- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_line"
<...more stuff...>
$ text                :List of 8
  ..$ family    : chr "Helvetica"
  ..$ face      : chr "plain"
  ..$ colour    : chr "black"
  ..$ size      : num 12
  ..$ hjust     : num 0.5
  ..$ vjust     : num 0.5
  ..$ angle     : num 0
  ..$ lineheight: num 0.9
  ..- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_text"
 $ axis.text           :List of 8
  ..$ family    : NULL
  ..$ face      : NULL
  ..$ colour    : chr "grey50"
  ..$ size      :Class 'rel'  num 0.8
  ..$ hjust     : NULL
  ..$ vjust     : NULL
  ..$ angle     : NULL
  ..$ lineheight: NULL
  ..- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_text"
<etc>


The reason I said I wanted a better way of changing things is because, from a user interface perspective, it seems inconsistent to create the elements with functions like element_text(), and then modify them as though they are list items.

-Winston

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: New theme system
parts: On Tue, May 29, 2012 at 6:42 AM, Kohske Takahashi <takahash...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Winston,

Nice work. I have one suggestion.
Now grob-oriented element (e.g., axis.title.x, plot.background, etc) and
parameter-oriented element (e.g., legend.position, panel.margin, etc)
is mixed within the same semantics.
It's somewhat confusing.
So how about explicitly separate them?

I agree that it is somewhat confusing. One thing I want to do is to merge some of the elements. For example, panel.margin could be merged into panel.background, as panel.background$margin. (Previously, this wasn't possible because panel.background was a function that returned a grob.)

Changes like this will break compatibility, though, and so I think it will have to wait until 0.10. The good thing is that it's now relatively easy to make these changes.

-Winston

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: New theme system
parts: - trying to install I get:

ERROR: package installation failed

Fixed.
- shouldn't title inherit from text? It does not on the graph

'title' is the title of the plot, as in "This is the title". 'plot.title' is probably what you're thinking of. These names probably could be improved in the future, but for now they have to remain the same to preserve backward compatibility.
- similarly, shouldn't legend.box inherit from rect?

From the help:
legend.box:A string specifying the direction of multiple guides. Possible string values are: "horizontal" and "vertical". 

I also find this name confusing...

- I don't see a difference between a line and a segment from the point of view of the user. Can they be merged in the UI (even if the grid functions called do actually draw axis ticks or grid lines are actually different)? Since there is no difference visually, to know what to change, the user would have to dive into theme_gray(). If we want to change stuff to keep it simple, this might be a good thing to prune out.

I completely agree. Previously they were separate because they returned different grobs, but now that they're just lists, it should be possible to get rid of element_segment() and use only element_line().

- I don't see a mechanism to force inheritance. Let us say I want all my lines to be black, because I intend to print in black and white purely. My first instinct would be to do
       line =  element_line(colour = "black")
but that does not change anything since this is already the default. Meanwhile, grid lines would still be white because the colour is specified at a lower level (panel.grid.major).
I would be nice, if feasible, to have something like the !important property in CSS, which overrides inheritance, like
       line =  element_line(colour = force("black"))
and now every line is black. Or even assume force() by default when using element_* functions : since the user is modifying the theme, he/she probably wants the instructions to be effective no matter what. There is still the possibility of direct access through the list for smaller modifications.

Hm... I'm not sure that this would be used often enough to justify the added complexity. In this example, you probably don't want every line to be black -- even in theme_bw, the grid lines are a light grey. I think you'd still have to create a new theme in this case.

- some text properties seem to be used only in legend: justification, align. Would it make sense to have them for all text elements (i.e. I want my axis labels to be left-aligned instead of centered)?

For most text elements, the way to do it is with element_text(hjust=1) or something like that. Hadley said that the legend alignment stuff (for example, legend.text.align) was there because text labels default to left-aligned and numbers default to right-aligned. I think that in the future, it would be good to get rid of legend.text.align, and instead use opts(legend.text = element_text(hjust=1)). They would also be able to use a special value, hjust="auto", to automatically left-align text and right-align numbers.



I just had another thought about the theming system -- with the new structure it could probably be used to store information about geom themes. For example, you could have the default geom_polygon have fill="gray90" and colour=NA.  Geoms that inherits from this, say, geom_boxplot, could override it with fill="white" and colour="black". But changes like this will probably have to wait until another big release.

-Winston

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: New theme system
parts:
Oh bother. I sent this to the wrong list.

On 5/29/2012 11:03 AM, Brian Diggs wrote:

> On 5/28/2012 10:07 PM, Winston Chang wrote:
>> Hi everyone -
>>
>> I've been working on the new theme system, based off the ideas Hadley
>> posted a while back. I think it's to the point where it's ready for some
>> feedback. Check it out and let me know if you have any comments or
>> suggestions:
>> https://github.com/wch/ggplot2/wiki/New-theme-system
>>
>> -Winston
>>
>

> I've just read the wiki page; I haven't looked at the code or even tried
> installing it (yet). But I wanted to give some feedback:
>
>
> The first thing, which I was VERY happy to see, was that you have a
> backwards compatibility layer with deprecation messages. Hopefully the
> message will point to the new (element_) function as well as a
> transition-guide like resource (even that wiki page would be good).
>
>
> I also like the element_*() renaming; the theme prefix meant two
> different things, and that confusion has been eliminated.
>
>
> I know that inheritance and single attribute updating were important
> goals for the new design, so it is good to see that in there. A nice way
> of specifying relative sizes is a nice addition. Gaining independent
> control over x and y axis attributes is good. Perhaps that can be
> further extended by having separate x/y versions of axis.ticks,
> axis.ticks.length, axis.ticks.margin, and axis.line.
>
>
> I am also glad that the implementation was not the start of the
> description and that (it seems) the requirement drove the
> implementation, and not the implementation driving the requirements.
>
>
> Does rel() work only with font sizes, or could it (does it) work with
> any numerical size. I'm thinking in particular margin/padding. Or any unit.
>
>
> In terms of the inheritance structure:
> * could legend.text and legend.title both inherit off of something off
> of text? The obvious name would be legend.text, but that doesn't work
> here since it is already being used.
> * Can the margins (legend.margin, panel.margin, axis.ticks.margin,
> plot.margin) inherit off a single margin, and maybe even use rel?
> * Should there be some sort of relationship between segment and line?
> They both have colour, size, and linetype. I'm thinking segment inherits
> from line.
> * There are two align's and a justification (legend.justification,
> legend.title.align, legend.text.align). I'm not sure what each take and
> whether they could be related (in an inheritance way) to each other.
> * What is the difference between legend.direction and legend.box? Both
> take "horizontal" or "vertical" as values.
> * Should the title text really be part of the theme? As I think about
> the themes, it seems like it shouldn't. If not, then there is the
> problem of where to put it. It is most similar to the labels of the
> scales, but it is really not a scale. Short of just making a dedicated
> function for it, or just putting it into labs(), I'm not sure what to do
> with it.
> * The only other elements that don't inherit from anything are:
> axis.ticks.length, legend.position, title, legend.direction, legend.box.
> I think that is fine; the first is a unit, but doesn't really relate to
> anything; maybe to the margin sizes if that becomes a set. The three
> legend bits are their own thing, and title is just a string.
>
>
> Is precedence well defined for things like:
>
> opts(axis.text = element_text(size=rel(0.5)),
> axis.text = element_text(size=4))
>
> That is, will it work and will it give a consistent result?
>
>
> Rather than modifying a theme directly as a list, why not utilize the
> existing opts() infrastructure for assignment? or update?
>
> mytheme <- theme_grey()
>
> mytheme <- update(mytheme, opts(text = element_text(family="Times",
> face="plain", colour="red", size=16, hjust=0.5, vjust=0.5, angle=0,
> lineheight=0.9)))
>
> or maybe
>
> mytheme <- opts(text = element_text(family="Times", face="plain",
> colour="red", size=16, hjust=0.5, vjust=0.5, angle=0, lineheight=0.9))
>
> although the latter would have to either specify everything or fall back
> to some defaults for unspecified things.
> The advantage of this approach is that it insulates the implementation,
> which isn't too hard since there already exists a way of specifying the
> structure (using element_*) independent of the implementation.
>
>
> How deep does relative sizing work? For instance:
>
> opts(text = element_text(size=16),
> axis.text = element_text(size=rel(0.5)),
> axis.text.x = element_text(size=rel(0.25)))
>
> What would the size of the text on the x axis be? 16*0.5*0.25=2 (rel's
> are multiplicative up the tree)? 16*0.5=8 (only the first rel going down
> the tree matters and any subsequent ones are ignored)? 16*0.25=4 (only
> the last rel in the tree matters, and it is in reference to the last
> absolute value)? I think the first one is what it should be.
>
>
> In general, I really like the new design. I think it fixes many problems
> of the old one, and I don't see any glaringly obvious problems with it.
>


--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University

On 30 May 2012 05:39, Winston Chang <winsto...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I just had another thought about the theming system -- with the new

> For example, you could have the default geom_polygon have fill="gray90" and
> colour=NA.  Geoms that inherits from this, say, geom_boxplot, could override
> it with fill="white" and colour="black".

Yes, please! That's something that's been bothering me forever in
ggplot2, that geoms and scales defaults cannot be conveniently tuned
to match the theme.

Regarding the inheritance of black lines, maybe we could use the
background (bg) and foreground (fg) concepts of beamer and have a flag
rel_col() that lightens or mutes the colour for example, so that black
lines in the theme fade into grey grid lines by defaut. rel_col()
could either play with the transparency, and/or do some colorspace
transformation to only alter the luminosity, or hue, or saturation.
rel() would be renamed rel_size(), obviously, and perhaps a few others
could follow this approach.

Cheers,

baptiste

PS: I only read the wiki page, not tried the code yet.

Say I have a plot "p" that I like, I want to be able to produce three
versions of this plot,

- version 1 is for a manuscript I'm writing, it needs to be in colour,
have serif fonts of size 12, and minimum line widths of 0.5 mm

p + theme_article(12, "serif")
## + lots of fiddling for each geom defaults

- version 2 is also for the same article, but for a black-and-white
print version

p + theme_articlebw(12, "serif")
## this doesn't change the colour scale, which I need to change manually:
## scale_colour_default <- scale_colour_grey

- version 3 is for a beamer presentation with a black background

p + theme_presentation(18)

## now the point sizes and line widths are too small compared to the
font size, I need to adjust all the geom defaults manually
## similarly, the colour scale that looked good on a white panel
background is now too muted on a dark background; again I need to
## change the default settings of the colour scale manually

Instead, I would like to have the theme change the default parameters
of geoms and scales, such as for example

low = "#132B43", high = "#56B1F7", na.value = "grey50" in
scale_colour_continuous

colour = "black", size = 0.5, linetype = 1, alpha = NA in

messages.subject: Re: New theme system
parts: Oops, forgot to reply all.
Does rel() work only with font sizes, or could it (does it) work with any numerical size. I'm thinking in particular margin/padding. Or any unit.
Right now it's only applied for fields named 'size'. It should work for units, although in the current implementation, there are no 'size' fields that are units.

In terms of the inheritance structure:
* could legend.text and legend.title both inherit off of something off of text? The obvious name would be legend.text, but that doesn't work here since it is already being used.

 
* Can the margins (legend.margin, panel.margin, axis.ticks.margin, plot.margin) inherit off a single margin, and maybe even use rel?

I think this is possible... but is it desirable? It looks like all of the margins are set to different values in theme_grey(). In the long term, the margins may be merged into other theme elements, which would break this inheritance. For example, panel.margin would become panel.background$margin or something like that.
* Should there be some sort of relationship between segment and line? They both have colour, size, and linetype.  I'm thinking segment inherits from line.
I just updated it -- the relationship is that element_segment is gone now. :)

* There are two align's and a justification (legend.justification, legend.title.align, legend.text.align). I'm not sure what each take and whether they could be related (in an inheritance way) to each other.

I think legend.justification is different from the other two. Maybe it could eventually be merged into legend.background...

The legend.title.align and legend.text.align properties are just strings, and I think inheritance currently won't work with strings. Also, I think they'll eventually go away and be folded into legend.title and legend.text.
* What is the difference between legend.direction and legend.box? Both take "horizontal" or "vertical" as values.
Good question - the ?opts page knows as much as I do.

* Should the title text really be part of the theme? As I think about the themes, it seems like it shouldn't. If not, then there is the problem of where to put it. It is most similar to the labels of the scales, but it is really not a scale. Short of just making a dedicated function for it, or just putting it into labs(), I'm not sure what to do with it.
I agree, the title should eventually be moved out of the theme. title() is already taken, but something like that would be good.

Is precedence well defined for things like:

opts(axis.text = element_text(size=rel(0.5)),
    axis.text = element_text(size=4))

That is, will it work and will it give a consistent result?

It's not "well-defined", but it works... It just uses the first one. On the other hand, if you do this, it uses the second one:
  opts(axis.text = element_text(size=rel(0.5))) +
  opts(axis.text = element_text(size=4))
Rather than modifying a theme directly as a list, why not utilize the existing opts() infrastructure for assignment? or update?

Maybe the + operator could be defined to work this way:
  mytheme <- theme_grey() + opts(axis.title= ...)
although the latter would have to either specify everything or fall back to some defaults for unspecified things.

Right, this is still a problem. For top-level items, you still can't just change the font family for mytheme$text -- you have to specify everything, with element_text(family="", face="", size="", colour="", ...)

How deep does relative sizing work?  For instance:

opts(text = element_text(size=16),
    axis.text = element_text(size=rel(0.5)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size=rel(0.25)))

What would the size of the text on the x axis be?  16*0.5*0.25=2 (rel's are multiplicative up the tree)? 16*0.5=8 (only the first rel going down the tree matters and any subsequent ones are ignored)? 16*0.25=4 (only the last rel in the tree matters, and it is in reference to the last absolute value)?  I think the first one is what it should be.
At each level of inheritance, it multiplies, so it would be 16*0.5*0.25=2.
In general, I really like the new design. I think it fixes many problems of the old one, and I don't see any glaringly obvious problems with it.
Great, thanks for the feedback!

It was early morning so I probably didn't have clear ideas...
The concept of rel_size() is quite clear: you want to specify the base
font size for the plot, and some particular elements such as the plot
title might be a bit bigger, or the axis labels slightly smaller
relative to this size.
This sort of family relationship could be extended to colours with
rel_col(). For example, if I specify that the background elements of
my plot (plot panel, strip panels, etc.) should be blue, then the grid
lines could default to a faded version of a complementary colour, for
example:

library(munsell)
library(grid)

rel_col <- function(x, complementary = TRUE, ...){
col <- as.numeric(col2rgb(x))
mnsl(lighter(complement(rgb2mnsl(col[1], col[2], col[3]), fix=TRUE)))
}

bg <- "cornflowerblue"
grid.newpage()
grid.rect(gp=gpar(fill=bg))
grid.grill(gp=gpar(col=fade(bg), lwd=4))

In the case of black foreground, instead of saying explicitely that
grid lines will be "grey95", and the panel border will be "grey50",
you could instead say rel_col(0.05) and rel_col(0.5) respectively, and
it would perform the interpolation to return the appropriate greys.
It's trivial for a grey scale, obviously, but less so for general
colours.

Cheers,

baptiste

While I agree that these functions would be useful, I think they would be better suited a more generic color-handling package, if that doesn't exist yet (I guess a combination of several packages can give the functionality now). And in that case, rather than rel_col (which, in the context of rel_size is understandable but is otherwise a bit cryptic) you would have alpha (as in scales), ligthen, darken, saturate, desaturate, etc. There's a stub of this in color-manip.r in scales.

This could probably expand on the work done in package colorspace: http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/colorspace/index.html , in particular to take advantage of the conversions between various colour representations.

>> "horizontal" or "vertical" as values.
>

Didn't think of looking at that page; it's been much improved since the
last time I looked at it (I had been relying on the wiki page).
legend.box talks about multiple guides, so that is probably the relevant
part.
